description: C as the language of the machine: types, pointers, memory, structures, files and the toolchain, taught by writing and debugging real systems-style programs. Taught to the depth of a leading systems programming course.
modelledOn: Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language
Bryant and O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (C and memory chapters)
King, C Programming: A Modern Approach
outcomes: Write well-structured C programs using the full type system, operators, control flow and functions.
Use arrays, strings and pointers correctly and explain their representation in memory.
Allocate and free dynamic memory and build linked structures without leaks or dangling pointers.
Model data with structures, unions and enumerations and persist it with text and binary files.
Drive the preprocessor, compiler, linker and debugger, and split a program across multiple files.
Find memory errors with tools such as a debugger and a sanitizer and reason about undefined behaviour.

units.title: C syntax, types and operators
topics: A first program; compiling with gcc or clang; the structure of a C program
Integer, character and floating types; sizes, ranges, signedness, overflow, limits.h
Constants, variables, declarations, initialisation; const and typedef
Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise and assignment operators; precedence; implicit conversions
printf and scanf formatting; getchar and putchar

units.title: Control flow and functions
topics: if, switch, while, do-while, for; break, continue, goto
Function definition and declaration, prototypes, header files
Call by value; scope, storage classes (auto, static, extern, register)
Recursion and the call stack; stack frames
Modular design: splitting a program into functions and files

units.title: Arrays and strings
topics: One- and multi-dimensional arrays; initialisation; array bounds and the danger of overrun
Strings as null-terminated char arrays; string.h functions and writing your own strlen, strcpy, strcmp
Passing arrays to functions; sizeof pitfalls
Sorting and searching arrays; a word-count and a Caesar cipher program

units.title: Pointers and memory
topics: Addresses, the & and * operators, pointer types, NULL
Pointer arithmetic and the equivalence of arrays and pointers; pointers to pointers
Call by reference with pointers; returning multiple values; swap
The memory map of a process: text, data, BSS, heap, stack
Dynamic memory: malloc, calloc, realloc, free; leaks, double free, use after free
Linked lists, stacks and a binary tree with dynamic nodes
Function pointers and callbacks; qsort

units.title: Structures, unions and enumerations
topics: Defining and using struct; nested structures; arrays of structures; the arrow operator
Memory layout, padding and alignment
Unions and tagged unions; bit fields; enum
Structures as records: a student register and an inventory program

units.title: File handling
topics: Streams: stdin, stdout, stderr; fopen, fclose and modes
Text I/O: fgets, fputs, fprintf, fscanf; line-by-line processing
Binary I/O: fread, fwrite, fseek, ftell; writing and reading records
Error handling with errno and perror; checking return values
Command-line arguments and processing a CSV file of sales data

units.title: The preprocessor and compilation
topics: #include, #define, macros with arguments and their pitfalls, conditional compilation, include guards
The pipeline: preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking; object files and libraries
Makefiles and building multi-file projects; static and shared libraries
Compiler flags, warnings as errors and optimisation levels

units.title: Debugging, safety and undefined behaviour
topics: gdb: breakpoints, stepping, inspecting memory and the stack
AddressSanitizer and Valgrind for leaks and invalid accesses
Undefined behaviour: uninitialised variables, signed overflow, buffer overflow and why it matters for security
Defensive coding, assertions and unit tests in C
Project: a small system utility or data manager combining files, structs and pointers
